what_its_for: This eye drop is a steroid medicine that helps reduce swelling, redness, itching, and discomfort in your eyes. It is used to treat eye inflammation (swelling), seasonal eye allergies, and to help your eyes heal after eye surgery.
how_to_take: Wash your hands well before using this medicine. Tilt your head back, pull down your lower eyelid gently to make a small pocket, and squeeze one drop into that pocket. Close your eye gently for 1 to 2 minutes — do not blink hard or rub your eye. If you wear contact lenses, take them out before using the drops and wait at least 15 minutes before putting them back in. If you are using other eye drops too, wait at least 5 to 10 minutes between each medicine. Shake the bottle well before each use if it is a suspension (cloudy drops).
dosing: The usual dose depends on why you are using it. For eye inflammation or after surgery, it is often 1 to 2 drops in the affected eye(s) 4 times a day. For allergies, it is usually 1 drop in each affected eye 4 times a day. Always follow your doctor or pharmacist's instructions exactly — do not use more or less than prescribed.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, use it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not double up or use extra drops to make up for a missed dose.
storage: Store this medicine at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep the bottle tightly closed when not in use. Do not freeze. Keep it out of reach of children. Throw away any unused medicine after the number of days your doctor recommends — usually 4 weeks after opening. Do not use it past the expiration date on the bottle.
what_to_avoid: Do not touch the dropper tip to your eye, fingers, or any surface, as this can contaminate the drops and cause an eye infection. Avoid wearing contact lenses while your eyes are inflamed or infected unless your doctor says it is okay. Do not drive or use machines right after putting in the drops if your vision is temporarily blurry — wait until you can see clearly.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you notice: sudden changes or worsening of your vision, eye pain that gets worse, increased redness or swelling of the eye, sensitivity to light, seeing halos around lights, or if your eye feels like something is stuck in it. Also call your doctor if your symptoms do not improve after a few days of treatment or if they get worse. Let your doctor know if you have a history of glaucoma (high eye pressure) or cataracts, as steroid eye drops can sometimes raise eye pressure.
when_it_works: You may start to notice some relief from redness, itching, and discomfort within a few days of starting treatment. However, continue using the drops for the full amount of time your doctor prescribed, even if you feel better. Do not stop early without talking to your doctor.
special_populations: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, trying to get pregnant, or breastfeeding before using this medicine. Use with caution in children — only use in kids if directed by a doctor. Older adults can generally use this medicine safely, but your doctor may want to monitor your eye pressure more closely. If you have a history of eye infections caused by viruses (like herpes), fungi, or bacteria, tell your doctor, as steroid eye drops can sometimes make certain infections worse.
